doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Reviews and critics
summary: Quotes on his website, a 'poor man's Eddie Jefferson' review, and the power of critics.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Times change. You know I was looking at some of the things people have said about you. This is from your website and it’s nice. You got a nice quote from Dave Brubeck.
You’ve got someone from the Topeka Journal said you were the Dennis Hopper of vocal jazz.
But he called you a musician. He says, “he’s not just a jazz singer, he’s a musician.” So that’s nice.
Have you seen reviews that aren’t as kind?

I’ve seen a couple. One of the very first travel gigs that I ever did, I was brand new. I did a festival in Clearwater, Florida. And I was a feature. I was a quick feature in the band and it was probably like a quartet. You know, rhythm section with a saxophone and a vibraphone, and I was part of it. And I was referred to as something like a “poor man’s Eddie Jefferson” or something like that. But you know what? I mean there are a lot of artists that I have heard say well I pay no attention to the reviews. It’s hard to do. I mean you take things personally. You can’t help it. We breathe. So it’s nice to read something that’s nice, and it’s not to read something that’s not. On the other hand, and, you know, sometimes someone will say something really nice about someone. And then they say something nice about someone else that’s like, I think they’re not happening. So what is the valid quotient here? Do you like everybody? Because if you like everybody then you’re just being kind you know, or you’re just doing the job. It’s my job to review, and I don’t want to say anything bad. Well then that kind of levels everything out. So I mean it’s personal. You know if you like what I do, solid. If you don’t, but then there’s the thing about like critics who review plays. What did I just see? I saw something. Oh, I just saw the film “Birdman.” Was it Birdman”? Yeah it was “Birdman.” I don’t know, it was something, a movie that I saw and the person who was in the play is — yeah it was “Birdman.” The person who was in the play approaches a theater critic, before the thing takes place. And the critic says to the star, he says, “listen,” he says, “I’m going to bury this thing.” He said, “you haven’t even seen it yet.” “I don’t like you and I don’t like your play. I haven’t seen it, and I’m going to close you down in a week.” Well they’ve got a lot of power. So if they want to they can turn a lot of people off to you. Or they can turn a lot of people on to you. So, you know, it’s kind of weird — I’m gassed, what people have written about me. But it’s kind of weird. You know, somebody’s got a lot of juice to be able to put the thumb on you if they want to.
Yeah, part of the business. I mean if you’re going to expose yourself to be out there then you’ve got to go along with that. It’s going to happen. Not everybody likes what everybody does.
